title: A geometric fibre of a map of spaces is connected exactly when every etale neighbourhood sees a connected ordinary fibre
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter spaces-more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms of Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file spaces-more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S and a geometric point ybar of Y, the geometric fibre X_{ybar} is connected if and only if for every etale neighbourhood (V, vbar) -> (Y, ybar) with V a scheme the base change X_V -> V has connected fibre X_v. The retained proof: the category of etale neighbourhoods of ybar is cofiltered with a cofinal system of schemes (Properties of Spaces, cofinal-etale), so reduce to Y a scheme with closed-under-reference point y; then X_y geometrically connected over kappa(y) iff X_{ybar} connected iff (X_y)_{k'} connected for every finite separable k'/kappa(y) (Spaces over Fields, geometrically-connected section and characterize-geometrically-disconnected); finally every finite separable extension is realized on residue fields by an affine etale neighbourhood (More on Morphisms, realize-prescribed-residue-field-extension-etale), which turns the finite-separable test into the quantifier over etale neighbourhoods. Retained author proof at lines 8107-8124.
